lessons.title: What Is Physics? Motion, Forces and Energy Around Us
lessons.focus: Define physics as study of matter, motion, forces, energy; tour school compound identifying physics at work (gate hinge, water tank, boda).
lessons.advanced: List three physics careers in Kenya (jua kali fabrication, civil engineering, radiography) and the physics each uses daily.

lessons.title: Science Safety and Workshop Rules
lessons.focus: Safe handling of sharps (panga, nails), heat (jiko), water, glass; agreeing class safety charter; why rules exist before experiments.
lessons.advanced: Write a risk assessment (hazard, risk, control) for three planned course builds.

lessons.title: The Scientific Investigation: Ask, Predict, Test, Record
lessons.focus: Steps of investigation using a swinging stone on a string; hypothesis writing; honest recording even when wrong.
lessons.advanced: Distinguish hypothesis from prediction; write both for the swing experiment.

lessons.title: Fair Tests and Variables
lessons.focus: Independent, dependent, controlled variables via dropping different balls (stone, rubber, crumpled paper ball) from same height.
lessons.advanced: Identify the confounding variable when two balls differ in BOTH mass and size.

lessons.title: SI Units and Why Standards Matter
lessons.focus: Metre, kilogram, second, litre; history of body-based measures (cubit, stride) and disputes at market without standards.
lessons.advanced: A trader sells a 'debe' of maize whose tin is dented inward. Quantify the buyer's loss if dent removes 8% of volume.

lessons.title: Measuring Length I: Rulers and Tape Measures
lessons.focus: mm/cm/m; correct ruler use (zero end, eye level); measure desk, book, classroom, footstride.
lessons.advanced: Classroom is 7.4 m long; convert to mm and explain when mm precision is pointless.

lessons.title: Measuring Length II: Vernier Callipers and Micrometers
lessons.focus: Jua kali precision tools; measuring wire diameter, nail thickness; reading a vernier scale.
lessons.advanced: Read a vernier to 0.1 mm; explain why the extra scale beats estimation.

lessons.title: Estimation Skills: Guess, Then Measure
lessons.focus: Estimating lengths/masses before measuring; calibration of the human estimator; flagpole height by shadows preview.
lessons.advanced: Flagpole shadow 6.0 m when your 1.5 m shadow is yours at height 1.6 m — compute pole height by similar triangles.

lessons.title: Measuring Mass: Build a Beam Balance
lessons.focus: Mass vs amount-of-matter; build ruler-on-pivot balance with debe/bottle-cap pans; compare masses of stones.
lessons.advanced: Why must the pans hang at equal distances from the pivot? Link to moments.

lessons.title: Weight vs Mass: A First Look
lessons.focus: Mass in kg is amount of matter; weight in N is gravity's pull; rubber-band spring balance shows weight changing, mass constant.
lessons.advanced: Your mass is 45 kg. State your weight on Earth (g=10 N/kg) and on the Moon (g=1.6 N/kg).

lessons.title: Measuring Time: Heartbeats, Stopwatches and Sundials
lessons.focus: Second as base unit; calibrating heartbeats against a clock; build stick-and-shadow sundial; limits of body clocks.
lessons.advanced: Why does a Kenyan sundial disagree with clock time across the year? Introduce the equation of time qualitatively.

lessons.title: Measuring Volume I: Regular Solids and Containers
lessons.focus: Volume = l×w×h; reading jerrican and sufuria markings; litre vs cm³ vs m³ conversions.
lessons.advanced: A '20-litre' jerrican measures 24×18×47 cm internally. Compute its true volume in litres and percentage error of the label.

lessons.title: Measuring Volume II: Displacement for Irregular Objects
lessons.focus: Stone volume by water displacement; overflow can made from a tin with a spout hole; Archimedes teaser.
lessons.advanced: A stone displaces 85 cm³ of water and weighs 2.1 N in air. Compute its density (take g=10 N/kg).
